adds isStubDataMode(), which the four data seams below call: stub data in production too, where the prototype has no backend, address book or reference data. Also changes isStubMode() itself to honour STUB_MODE in production, by design (Sam's decision): the deployed prototype signs in exactly like a local `npm run dev` — stub sign-in, open to anyone who reaches it unless PROTOTYPE_PASSWORD puts the prototype's own shared password in front (src/server/prototype-password) — unless STUB_MODE=false restores plants-frontend's own Defra ID sign-in. Covered by src/server/prototype-sets/production-run.test.js
picks the stub records store with isStubDataMode() in place of isStubMode(), so production keeps stub records

serves the stub countries with isStubDataMode() in place of isStubMode(), so production never calls reference data; also wraps the stub labels with the src/server/prototype-data overlay (withExtraCountries), one import and one declaration, so a set's extra countries come after the stub rows

serves the stub ports with isStubDataMode() in place of isStubMode(), so production never calls reference data; also wraps the stub ports with the src/server/prototype-data overlay (withExtraPorts), one import and one declaration, so a set's extra ports come after the stub rows

expects the prototype's development auth cookie name, so a local prototype and a local plants-frontend do not overwrite each other's sign-in; one describe block pinning the Defra ID redirect and sign-out redirect defaults to port 3103; and a test proving TRADE_IMPORTS_INS_FRONTEND_URL is ignored, so the address book link's dead default cannot be overridden

The house conventions a designer's change must meet, checked by lint

the 'journeys' project's testMatch was broadened to admit the sets-chooser boot-check spec, and the web server sets PROTOTYPE_SEED=false so every spec's dashboard starts empty; plus an opt-in 'walkthroughs' project (PROTOTYPE_WALKTHROUGHS=true) for fit/walkthroughs, and PLAYWRIGHT_RECORD_EVERYTHING=true turning video, trace and screenshots on for every project, for the published report. The walkthroughs project's slowMo now defaults to 0 (human pacing is explicit, in scripts/designer/walkthrough/pace.js and human-pace.js, not from slowMo), its timeout is 600 000ms (long enough for a human-paced walk of the longest story), and it alone runs with bypassCSP: true, because the human-pace cursor overlay's CSSOM style writes are inline styles under the prototype's CSP and every story failed on that without it
